payload.reason: The evidence indicates that analyzing self-attention functions in the last layer of the BERT model is justified due to the stability of attention correlations across tasks and the limited changes in attention functions during fine-tuning. Additionally, the last layer's attention heads show weaker correlations compared to attention flow, suggesting that raw attention weights may not effectively represent token relevance.

claims.text: The last layer of BERT shows stable attention correlations across tasks, indicating its relevance for analysis.
Fine-tuning does not significantly change the attention functions in BERT, supporting the focus on the last layer.
Attention heads in the last layer produce weaker correlations than attention flow, suggesting limited utility for direct analysis.
